correctness.rationale: Uniform-volume on P_m(c) equals normalized iid Exp(1) coordinates conditioned on scale-invariant E=max Y≤c min Y. The minimum density is m exp(-my)(1-exp(-(c−1)y))^(m−1); Z=exp(-(c−1)min Y) transforms exactly to Beta(m/(c−1),m), mean 1/c and variance (c−1)^2/[c²(mc+c−1)]. Given minimum and index the other entries are iid truncated Exp on [y,cy]. Conditional LLN plus independent Gamma(m,1) sum proves the ν_c empirical weak limit, exchangeability gives fixed-k propagation of chaos, endpoint sampling gives both extremes. Direct integration verifies mean 1, second moment 2-c(log c/(c−1))² and radius 1-c(log c/(c−1))²; deterministic scaled coordinate bounds [1/c,c] upgrade to L^q. Verified moment formulas independently at c=1.001,1.5,2,3,10; no finite simulation used to prove asymptotics.
residual_risks: Only c>1 fixed; no varying-ratio or extreme-value fluctuation law.

value.rationale: Central simplex polytopes are natural high-dimensional convex bodies whose volume and faces were studied. A typical uniform-volume point law, asymptotic independence, boundary localization and sharp Euclidean radius determine genuinely different geometry from volume or Hausdorff extremal values. The c=2 constant answers an explicit rescaling motivation.

limitations: Fixed c>1; uniform Hausdorff volume distribution only; no varying c_m, no rate, no whole-polytope convergence.
